source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Fundamental theorem of linear maps
statement: For a linear map on a finite-dimensional domain, domain dimension equals null-space dimension plus range dimension.
conclusion: dim V = dim null T + dim range T, and range T is finite-dimensional.
typical_uses: Convert injectivity, surjectivity, and dimension questions into rank-nullity equations.
common_misuses: Applying rank-nullity when the domain is infinite-dimensional.
Confusing the range dimension with the codomain dimension.
bridge_lemmas: Extend a basis of null T to a basis of V and map the added vectors.
repair_templates: State finite-dimensionality of V and replace an unsupported rank claim by dim V=dim null T+dim range T.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Invertibility iff injective and surjective
statement: A linear map has a two-sided linear inverse exactly when it is both injective and surjective.
conclusion: T is invertible iff T is injective and surjective; the inverse is unique.
typical_uses: Repair inverse constructions by proving both one-to-one and onto properties.
common_misuses: Using a one-sided inverse as a two-sided inverse without finite-dimensional hypotheses or a separate argument.
bridge_lemmas: Surjectivity gives unique preimages only after injectivity is known; linearity of the inverse follows from uniqueness.
repair_templates: Add separate injectivity and surjectivity proofs, then define the inverse by unique preimages.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Dimension of a quotient space
statement: The quotient by a subspace has dimension equal to ambient dimension minus subspace dimension.
conditions: U is a subspace of V.
typical_uses: Count degrees of freedom after imposing a subspace relation.
common_misuses: Treating cosets as individual vectors or omitting finite-dimensionality in dimension arithmetic.
bridge_lemmas: The quotient map has kernel U and image V/U.
repair_templates: Introduce the quotient map and apply rank-nullity.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Dual injectivity and surjectivity criteria
statement: For finite-dimensional spaces, T is surjective iff its dual is injective, and T is injective iff its dual is surjective; dual maps preserve rank.
conclusion: T surjective iff T' injective; T injective iff T' surjective; dim range T'=dim range T.
typical_uses: Transfer a difficult range argument to a null-space argument for the dual map.
common_misuses: Reversing the direction of the dual map or forgetting finite-dimensionality for the converse criteria.
bridge_lemmas: null T' equals the annihilator of range T; range T' equals the annihilator of null T.
repair_templates: Write the correct dual domain W'->V' and invoke annihilator identities before concluding injectivity or surjectivity.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Root-factor and zero bound
statement: A root lambda of a degree-m polynomial is equivalent to divisibility by z-lambda; a nonzero degree-m polynomial has at most m distinct roots.
conditions: p is a nonzero polynomial over a field F.
conclusion: p(lambda)=0 iff p=(z-lambda)q with deg q=m-1, and p has at most m roots in F.
typical_uses: Factor annihilating polynomials and bound eigenvalue counts.
common_misuses: Applying the root bound to the zero polynomial or counting multiplicities as distinct roots.
repair_templates: Separate the zero polynomial case, then factor one root and induct on degree.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are independent
statement: Any list of eigenvectors associated with pairwise distinct eigenvalues is linearly independent.
conditions: v_j are eigenvectors for pairwise distinct eigenvalues.
conclusion: The list v_j is linearly independent.
typical_uses: Bound the number of eigenvalues and build eigenvector bases.
common_misuses: Allowing repeated eigenvalues or zero vectors.
bridge_lemmas: Apply T-lambda_m I to a minimal dependence relation.
repair_templates: Group repeated eigenvalues separately and apply the result only across distinct eigenvalues.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Minimal polynomial divisibility criterion
statement: There is a unique monic least-degree polynomial p with p(T)=0, and q(T)=0 exactly when p divides q.
conditions: T acts on a finite-dimensional vector space.
conclusion: deg p<=dim V and q(T)=0 iff q=p s for some polynomial s.
typical_uses: Test operator identities and constrain possible eigenvalues or canonical forms.
common_misuses: Using a nonmonic annihilating polynomial as the minimal polynomial or inferring divisibility without polynomial division.
bridge_lemmas: Divide q by p and show a nonzero remainder would contradict minimality.
repair_templates: Normalize to monic p, perform Euclidean division q=ps+r, and prove r(T)=0 forces r=0.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Equivalent criteria for diagonalizability
statement: An operator is diagonalizable iff its domain has an eigenvector basis, equivalently the sum of distinct eigenspaces is direct and exhaustive, equivalently its minimal polynomial splits into distinct linear factors.
conditions: T acts on a finite-dimensional vector space.
conclusion: The listed diagonalizability conditions are equivalent.
typical_uses: Repair claims that eigenvalues alone imply diagonalizability by checking eigenspace dimensions or minimal-polynomial multiplicities.
common_misuses: Assuming distinct eigenvalues are necessary, or ignoring repeated roots in the minimal polynomial.
bridge_lemmas: Distinct-eigenvalue eigenspaces form a direct sum.
repair_templates: Compute the minimal polynomial or compare the sum of eigenspace dimensions with dim V.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization
statement: Subtract successive orthogonal projections from a linearly independent list and normalize; the resulting orthonormal list preserves each initial span.
conditions: v1,...,vm is linearly independent in an inner product space.
conclusion: The procedure yields orthonormal e1,...,em with span(v1,...,vk)=span(e1,...,ek) for every k.
typical_uses: Construct orthonormal bases and repair projection or QR arguments.
common_misuses: Dividing by zero when the input list is dependent or using the wrong inner-product slot in complex spaces.
bridge_lemmas: Independence implies each residual f_k is nonzero.
repair_templates: Check independence first, then subtract projections onto all prior normalized vectors and normalize.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Finite-dimensional Riesz representation
statement: Every linear functional on a finite-dimensional inner-product space is uniquely inner product with one vector.
conclusion: There is a unique v in V with phi(u)=<u,v> for every u.
typical_uses: Convert functional equations into vector equations and construct adjoints.
common_misuses: Applying the theorem to arbitrary infinite-dimensional spaces without continuity/completeness assumptions.
bridge_lemmas: Use an orthonormal basis and v=sum phi(e_j)e_j.
repair_templates: Add finite-dimensionality or a suitable Hilbert-space continuity hypothesis before invoking representation.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Orthogonal decomposition and projection
statement: For a finite-dimensional subspace U, V=U direct-sum U-perp; every v has a unique decomposition v=P_U v+w with w orthogonal to U, and P_U is linear and idempotent.
conditions: U is a subspace of V.
conclusion: V=U orthogonal direct sum U-perp; P_U is the unique orthogonal projection onto U and ||v-P_Uv|| is minimal over U.
typical_uses: Repair least-squares, closest-point, and orthogonality proofs.
common_misuses: Assuming U plus U-perp equals V in infinite dimensions without closure, or confusing orthogonal and algebraic projections.
bridge_lemmas: Gram-Schmidt gives an orthonormal basis of U and projection is sum <v,e_j>e_j.
repair_templates: Explicitly decompose v into its U and U-perp components and invoke Pythagoras for minimality.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Spectral theorem
statement: A real self-adjoint operator or complex normal operator on a finite-dimensional inner-product space has an orthonormal eigenbasis.
conditions: T is self-adjoint over R, or normal over C.
conclusion: V is the orthogonal direct sum of eigenspaces and T is unitarily diagonalizable; all eigenvalues are real in the self-adjoint case.
typical_uses: Justify orthonormal diagonalization, positivity, square roots, and singular-value arguments.
common_misuses: Applying the theorem to arbitrary operators or to a real normal operator without self-adjointness.
repair_templates: Check normality/self-adjointness and the field before invoking an orthonormal eigenbasis.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Singular value decomposition
statement: Every linear map between finite-dimensional inner-product spaces is a sum of rank-one maps along orthonormal domain and range lists, weighted by positive singular values.
conditions: T:V->W is linear between finite-dimensional inner-product spaces.
conclusion: There are orthonormal e_k,f_k and s_k>0 such that T v=sum s_k <v,e_k> f_k; s_k are square roots of eigenvalues of T*T.
typical_uses: Analyze rank, null spaces, pseudoinverses, and low-rank approximations.
common_misuses: Treating singular values as eigenvalues of T or omitting zero singular values when discussing injectivity.
bridge_lemmas: T*T is positive, null(T*T)=null T, and its positive eigenspaces generate the decomposition.
repair_templates: Form T*T, apply the spectral theorem, normalize T e_k by s_k, and extend lists orthonormally.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Generalized eigenspace decomposition
statement: Over C, a finite-dimensional operator decomposes its space as a direct sum of generalized eigenspaces, each invariant, with T-lambda I nilpotent on its summand.
conditions: V is finite-dimensional complex vector space.
T is an operator on V.
conclusion: V=direct sum G(lambda,T) over distinct eigenvalues; G(lambda,T)=null(T-lambda I)^{dim V}.
typical_uses: Repair diagonalization failures and reduce operator questions to nilpotent blocks.
common_misuses: Using generalized eigenspaces over R when eigenvalues do not split, or replacing direct sum by ordinary sum.
bridge_lemmas: Powers of an operator have ascending null spaces and descending ranges that stabilize by dim V.
repair_templates: Factor the minimal polynomial over C, define G(lambda,T) as a stabilized null space, then prove directness via generalized-eigenvector independence.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Cayley-Hamilton theorem
statement: An operator over C annihilates its characteristic polynomial.
conditions: T acts on a finite-dimensional complex vector space.
q is the characteristic polynomial of T.
conclusion: q(T)=0; hence the characteristic polynomial is a multiple of the minimal polynomial.
typical_uses: Derive operator identities and bound powers or inverses using characteristic-polynomial coefficients.
common_misuses: Using the theorem before defining the characteristic polynomial or over an arbitrary field without a corresponding split definition.
bridge_lemmas: On each generalized eigenspace, the appropriate nilpotent power vanishes; combine via direct-sum decomposition.
repair_templates: Decompose into generalized eigenspaces and show each factor of q(T) kills its corresponding summand.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Determinant multiplicativity and invertibility
statement: The determinant is multiplicative, and an operator or square matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero; eigenvalues satisfy det(lambda I-T)=0.
conditions: S,T are endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional vector space, or A,B are same-size square matrices.
conclusion: det(ST)=det S det T; T invertible iff det T !=0; lambda is an eigenvalue iff det(lambda I-T)=0.
typical_uses: Convert matrix invertibility or eigenvalue claims into scalar determinant equations.
common_misuses: Assuming det(S+T)=det S+det T or applying determinant to rectangular maps.
bridge_lemmas: Use the one-dimensional space of top-degree alternating forms and the invertibility criterion.
repair_templates: Replace additive determinant manipulation with multiplicativity and check square-size hypotheses.

source: Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Tensor product basis and universal property
statement: Tensor products of bases form a basis, and bilinear maps VxW->U correspond uniquely to linear maps V tensor W->U.
conclusion: dim(V tensor W)=dim V dim W; e_j tensor f_k is a basis when e_j,f_k are bases; there is a unique linear Gamma-hat with Gamma-hat(v tensor w)=Gamma(v,w).
typical_uses: Linearize bilinear constructions and prove tensor identities by checking basis tensors.
common_misuses: Treating every tensor as a single pure tensor or assuming pure-tensor representations are unique.
bridge_lemmas: Evaluate a proposed tensor identity on dual-basis pairs, or check it on basis tensors and extend linearly.
repair_templates: Use the universal property rather than choosing arbitrary decompositions into pure tensors.
